factual_methodological.summary: Official U.S. Treasury data confirm the 23 September closes at 4.31% (2Y), 5.11% (10Y) and 5.40% (30Y), versus 4.26%, 4.96% and 5.29% on 22 September. Current event and market claims are explicitly separated from inference and scenarios; the report qualifies the single-auction signal and survey-to-GDP limitation.

taxonomy.summary: Program, related program, dimensions, geography, topics and phenomena use controlled taxonomy values; phenomena is a valid array.

translation.summary: EN and PT-BR preserve the same thesis, market levels, qualifications, causal mechanisms, scenarios and visual semantics; PT-BR is naturally localized.

editorial_publication_readiness.summary: The opening states the new thesis directly; headings name mechanisms rather than template categories; prose contains no exposed QA/prompt scaffolding; prior oil-relief material is demoted to background and the dominant novelty is the cross-border sovereign-duration repricing; progression runs from thesis through U.S. evidence, transmission, Japan, energy, diplomacy, dislocations and synthesis.

contextual_depth.summary: The report incorporates the institutional context needed for the mechanism: Fed policy, Treasury supply absorption, BOJ normalization, Japanese currency/import-price transmission, Gulf logistics and U.S.-China policy channels, without adding ornamental history.

visual_evidence_readiness.signature: 1 analytical table + 1 single-unit Treasury bar chart + 1 causal flow + 1 geographic transmission map
visual_evidence_readiness.summary: Visuals are analytical rather than decorative, preserve units and dimensional compatibility, represent mechanisms stated in the prose, and have semantic EN/PT-BR parity.
visual_evidence_readiness.limitations: The geographic visual is a qualitative transmission map rather than a geospatial magnitude map; the Treasury chart is a same-date cross-maturity comparison, not a time series.

novelty_repetition.summary: The candidate explicitly compares the 21-23 September editions and identifies a material new mechanism: a 15 bp one-day rise in the official U.S. 10-year yield to 5.11%, weak five-year auction reception and immediate spillover to Japanese duration. Oil relief is retained only where the renewed crude/product stress interacts with rates.

contrary_evidence: A single weak Treasury auction does not establish a durable demand regime.
Flash PMI strength does not guarantee equally strong realized GDP or renewed inflation acceleration.
Improved Gulf crude logistics remain a source of physical relief even as refined-product stress and geopolitical optionality persist.
The tightening-regime thesis would weaken if long yields retrace on better auction demand, activity fails to confirm the flash PMI, or refinery/product trade normalizes.
limitations: Intraday Japanese bond, FX and futures-implied probability observations are time-sensitive snapshots and rely on contemporaneous market reporting.

The causal decomposition of the long-end move among nominal growth, term premium, supply absorption and inflation uncertainty is analytical inference rather than a directly observed allocation of basis points.
The Trump-Xi meeting is treated as a catalyst until implemented policy outcomes are observable.
